claims.sourceText: Letter from Puthoff reported by M.J. Banias, Vice, 14 November 2019
claims.text: Puthoff wrote in 2012 that testing of the Linda Moulton Howe metal samples had not proved alien origin nor produced any 'interesting/anomalous outcome', but that one further test requiring unavailable equipment remained.

a.label: ADAM Research Project (Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials)

edges.label: Samples routed to laboratories founded by Puthoff
edges.note: TTSA partnered with Puthoff-founded laboratories to study the ADAM materials; Puthoff had already tested the same Howe samples privately, reporting in a 2012 letter that no anomalous outcome had been obtained.

a.label: ADAM Research Project (Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials)

edges.label: Custody chain: anonymous source to Art Bell, to Linda Moulton Howe, to Carnegie DTM (1996), to Puthoff, to TTSA (2019), to the US Army
edges.note: Howe says the samples were tested by Carnegie Science's Department of Terrestrial Magnetism in 1996 and by Puthoff on several later occasions before TTSA bought them for $35,000 in 2019.

edges.label: Private, non-FOIA-able laboratory sitting between a government programme and a public company
edges.note: EarthTech has published no analytical results on the samples it has held, and as a private corporation is outside FOIA. Every documented chain that reaches it stops there.
